overall_summary: The channel's performance is heavily driven by immersive, first-person hypothetical space scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme planetary facts, which consistently cross the 800-1,000 views threshold. Conversely, general psychology facts, brain-related content, and repetitive space facts (e.g., space silence, old stars) struggle to gain traction, rarely exceeding 100 views. Extending the video duration from 15-16 seconds to 19-21 seconds has also correlated with a significant rise in views and engagement metrics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' achieved 1,024 views and 38 likes; 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' reached 970 views; 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' hit 821 views.
winning_patterns.action: Pivot the space content strategy to focus on first-person survival scenarios on extreme exoplanets, using high-stakes 'What If' framing.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Planetary Phenomena with Sensationalist Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' reached 1,025 views; 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' reached 1,055 views; 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' reached 721 views.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight bizarre weather, composition, or physical rules of exoplanets using high-contrast, curiosity-inducing titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' got only 10 views; 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' got 17 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' got 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause production on standard cognitive psychology and brain trick videos, as they fail to capture the interest of the current algorithmic seed audience.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' generated only 33 and 87 views across multiple uploads; 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' got 11 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid basic, textbook-style space facts that lack a narrative hook or a visual/visceral threat element.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Planet of Supersonic Rubies?
next_video.opening_direction: If you fell into planet HAT-P-7b, you wouldn't just burn—you'd be shredded by a supersonic storm of actual rubies and sapphires.
next_video.twist_direction: But the real nightmare is the night side, where winds reach 10,000 miles per hour, turning these precious gems into deadly, razor-sharp bullets.
next_video.reason: Combines the highly successful 'What If You Fell Into...' format with the proven high-performing concept of the ruby-raining planet (721 views), utilizing the optimal 21-second duration.

experiment: Test a 'What If' survival scenario based on extreme ocean depths or deep-earth mysteries (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into the Mariana Trench's Hidden Underworld?') to see if the first-person survival format translates successfully to geography and oceanography.
